instruction: Start playing a playlist on Spotify that has enough songs for my workout today. I do not want to have to change the playlist in the middle of my workout. The workout plan is in Simple Note.
notes: Two-app task (simple_note + spotify) with phone.get_current_date_and_time used to learn today's weekday (2023-05-25 is a Thursday) so the right day's duration_mins can be parsed from the workout note. The note is found via search_notes(query='workout') and read via show_note, which yields the workout duration knowledge (found-workout-duration). On Spotify, show_playlist_library reveals playlists and their song_ids; the song object long-enough-playlist-songs is a placeholder for all song ids of the candidate playlist (show_song is invoked per id at runtime and durations summed). The numeric comparison sum(duration)/60 >= duration_mins is abstracted by the knowledge predicate playlist-fits-workout, asserted by spotify-show-song once the workout duration is known; the playlist object itself is bound by the selection rule 'first library playlist whose total duration suffices'. play_music with that playlist_id sets the player playing with exactly that playlist's songs in the queue, matching the evaluation (only spotify.MusicPlayer changes, is_playing true, queue duration >= workout minutes, queue ids == playlist ids). The goal is the nullary workout-playlist-playing (only achievable by playing a fitting playlist) plus task-completed; complete_task takes no answer since the task asks no question.
